Rashi on Shabbat 53a:10:1.hebrew: מאי שנא מאוכף - שאסור ליטול, וכ"ש להניחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:10:1.english: How is it different from a saddle - For it is forbidden to remove [it], and all the more so to place [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:10:2.hebrew: דנפיל ממילא - כדקתני: מוליכו ומביאו לחצר, והוא נופל מאליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:10:2.english: That it falls on its own - As [the baraita] taught: He leads it back and forth in the courtyard, and it falls on its own.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:11:1.hebrew: כאן לחממה - מרדעת צריך לחממה, ומותר משום צער דצינה. אבל נטילת אוכף אינו אלא שיצטנן — שנתחממה ע"י משאוי שנשאה מבעוד יום — ואי לא שקיל ליה, לא איכפת לן, שהרי הוא יצטנן מאליו, דאמרי אינשי וכו':
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:11:1.english: Here, to warm it - [A] saddlecloth is needed to warm [the animal], and is permitted on account of the suffering from cold. But the removal of a saddle is only so that [the animal] will cool down — for it became heated by means of the burden that it carried while it was still day — and if he does not remove it, we do not care, for it will cool down on its own, as people say, etc.:

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:1.hebrew: בזנב שועל - שתולין לו בין עיניו, שלא ישלוט בו עין:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:1.english: With a fox's tail - Which they hang between its eyes, so that the [evil] eye will not have power over it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:2.english: A crimson ribbon - [It is] for ornament.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:3.hebrew: בכיס שלו - שתולין לו באמתו לקבל זוב ולבדוק מנין ראיותיו, שאינו תכשיט לו:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:3.english: With his pouch - Which they hang on his member to collect the discharge and to check the number of his emissions, for it is not an ornament for him.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:4.hebrew: בכיס שבדדיהן - לקבל חלב הנוטף; אי נמי, שלא ישרטו דדיהן על הקוצים, שהיו דדיהן גסין:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:4.english: With a pouch that is on their udders - To catch the milk that drips [from them]; or alternatively, so that their udders will not be scratched on thorns, as their udders were large.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:5.hebrew: בחסום שבפיה - שחוסמין אותה שלא תרעה בשדות אחרים, וכשמגיעין למקום מרעיתם נוטלין אותה הימנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:5.english: With the muzzle that is on its mouth - For they muzzle it so that it will not graze in others' fields, and when they arrive at their pasture, they remove it from it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:6.hebrew: בסנדל שברגליה - שעושין לה סנדל של מתכת, שלא יזיקוה האבנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:6.english: With a shoe that is on its feet - For they make a metal shoe for it, so that the stones will not injure it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:7.english: An amulet - A writing for the healing of illness.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:8.english: Proven effective - That has already healed three times.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:9.hebrew: וזה חומר בבהמה מבאדם - קס"ד השתא דאקמיע קאי, דאמרינן לקמן בפרק במה אשה יוצאה (שבת ד' סא.) שהאדם יוצא בקמיע מומחה. וכל הני דקתני לא תצא — הנך דלאו שמירת גופה הוא, אלא משאוי; וסנדל — משום דדילמא מישתליף, ואתי לאתויי:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:12:9.english: And this is a stricture in an animal more than in a person - It enters our minds now that [this] refers to the amulet, for we say later in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Isha Yotzah (Shabbat 61a) that a person may go out with an effective amulet. And all those [other items concerning which] it teaches, "It may not go out" — those are not protection of its body, but rather a burden; and a shoe [is forbidden] because it might slip off and [the owner] will come to carry it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:1.english: A bandage that is on a wound - There is no [reason] to say [that] he might come to carry it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:2.hebrew: קשישין שעל השבר - בהמה שנשבר בה עצם, עושין לה דפין מכאן ומכאן וקושרים אותן שם, והן מעמידין העצם שלא ינוד אנה ואנה עד שמתחבר:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:2.english: Splints that are on a broken bone - An animal in which a bone was broken — they make boards for it on this side and on that side and tie them there, and they hold the bone in place so that it does not move to and fro until it knits.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:3.english: And with the afterbirth dangling from it - Where part of it has emerged.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:4.hebrew: ופוקקין לה זוג - אבל כשאינו פקוק, אפי' בחצר לא תצא, מפני שהעינבל שבתוכה מקשקש ומוליד קול. לכך פוקק בצמר או במוכין, שלא יקשקש העינבל שבתוכה:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:4.english: And one may plug the bell for it - But when it is not plugged, it may not go out even into a courtyard, because the clapper inside it rattles and produces sound. Therefore, one plugs [it] with wool or with soft rags, so that the clapper inside it will not rattle.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:6.english: A clapper - [In Old French:] bateil [the clapper of a bell].

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:7.hebrew: ומטיילת - באותו זוג בחצר, אבל לא תצא בו לרה"ר, כדמפרש לקמן בפרקין (שבת דף נד:), דמיחזי כמאן דאזיל לחינגא:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:13:7.english: And [it] may walk - With that bell in the courtyard, but it may not go out with it into the public domain, as is explained later in our chapter (Shabbat 54b), that it appears like one who is going to the market.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:14:1.hebrew: מאי לאו - בסייחים גדולים קאמר, דצוארן ארוך ואין להם צער לשוח ולאכול מע"ג הקרקע, ותולה להן טרסקל לתענוג — וקשיא לשמואל:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:14:1.english: What, is it not: It is speaking of large foals, whose necks are long and they have no distress in bending down and eating from off the ground, and one hangs a basket for them for pleasure — and [this is] a difficulty for Shmuel.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:15:1.hebrew: קטנים - ארכובותיהן גבוהין וצוארן קטן, ויש להם צער לשוח ע"ג הקרקע ולאכול:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:15:1.english: Small [foals] - Their knees are high and their neck is short, and it causes them discomfort to bend down to the ground and eat.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:1:1.english: Our mishna is also precise - [This is taught] later in this chapter.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:3:1.english: Even with the saddle - For it also helps to warm it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:3:2.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יקשור לו מסריכן - פוטרא"ל, דמיחזי כמי שרוצה להטעינו משוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:3:2.english: Provided that he does not tie its masrikhan - [Old French: poitrel, a breast-strap,] for it appears like one who wants to load a burden onto it.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:3:3.hebrew: רצועה תחת זנבו - פושל"א, שנותנים שם שלא תרד האוכף והמשוי על צוארה כשהיא יורדת לעמק, והמסרך — שלא תרד על זנבה כשהיא עולה על ההרים:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:3:3.english: A strap under its tail - *Posle* [a crupper], which they place there so that the saddle and the load do not slip onto its neck when it goes down into a valley; and the *masrakh* [breastcollar is] so that it does not slip onto its tail when it goes up mountains.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:4:1.hebrew: מהו ליתן מרדעת - ולא לצאת לרה"ר, אלא בחצר, ומפני הצינה:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:4:1.english: What is [the law regarding] placing a saddlecloth - And not to go out into the public domain, but [rather] in a courtyard, and on account of the cold.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:4:2.hebrew: ה"ג - אמר ליה: מותר. א"ל: וכי מה בין זה לאוכף? אישתיק:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:4:2.english: This is the correct reading: “He said to him: [It is] permitted. He said to him: And what is the difference between this and a saddle? He remained silent.”

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:5:1.hebrew: איתיביה כו' - כסבור: הא דאישתיק משום דלא אשגח ביה, דסבר אוכף נמי שרי — ואותיביה מברייתא דאסור ליטלה. והשתא: ליטול אמרת לא, להניח מיבעי'? דדמי כאילו צריך להטעינה משוי:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:5:1.english: He raised an objection, etc. - [Rav Asi] thought that the reason [Rabbi Ḥiyya] remained silent was because he did not pay attention to him, as he thought that a saddle, too, is permitted; so he raised an objection to him from a baraita, [stating] that it is forbidden to remove it. And now: [if regarding] removing [it], you said no, is [forbidding one to] place [it] necessary? For it looks as though he needs to load it with a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:6:1.english: In accordance with his teacher - Rav.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:6:2.hebrew: טרסקל - סל מלא שעורים תולין לה בצוארה, ופיה נתון לתוכו ואוכלת. ותענוג בעלמא הוא — שלא תטרח לשוח צוארה לארץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:6:2.english: A basket - A basket full of barley that they hang around its neck, and its mouth is placed inside it and it eats. And it is mere pleasure — so that it does not have to trouble [itself] to bend its neck to the ground.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:7:1.hebrew: מרדעת מותר - דצערא היא, הלכך אורחה בהכי, ולאו משוי הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:7:1.english: A saddlecloth is permitted - For it is [to prevent] suffering; therefore, this is its normal manner, and it is not a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:7:2.english: The ruling of Rav - That he permits [going out with] a basket:

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:7:3.hebrew: אבא - חברי, כמו: "אברך" — "אבא למלכא" (בראשית מא):
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:7:3.english: Abba - [Meaning] my colleague, like [the translation of] “Avrekh” [as] “father to the king” (Genesis 41).

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:8:1.hebrew: שמואל קרי אריוך, על שם שהיה בקי בדינין ושופט כמלך השופט על הארץ — לשון ריכא, מלך (ב"ב דף ד.):
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:8:1.english: [He] calls Shmuel "Aryokh" because he was expert in [civil] laws and judged like a king who judges over the land — [from the] expression reikha, [meaning] king (Bava Batra 4a).

Rashi on Shabbat 53a:9:1.hebrew: והא רב נמי אמרה - דכיון דשרי בטרסקל, כ"ש מרדעת:
Rashi on Shabbat 53a:9:1.english: And didn't Rav also say it? - For since he permitted a basket, all the more so a saddlecloth [is permitted].

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:14:1.hebrew: מאי לאו בגדולים ומשום תענוג - וא"ת: ומאי קושיא? דילמא הכא מיירי בטרסקל שנתלה מע"ש, אבל לתלות בשבת — אפי' בחצר אסור! ותירץ: דדייק מדנקט רה"ר גבי טרסקל טפי משאר, דכולהו נמי ברה"ר איירי; אלא נקט רה"ר — דבחצר מותר בכל ענין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:14:1.english: What? Is it not [referring] to large [foals] and for pleasure - And if you say: But what is the difficulty? Perhaps here it is dealing with a basket that was hung from the eve of Shabbat, but to hang [it] on Shabbat, even in a courtyard is forbidden! And [one can] answer that [the Gemara] deduces this from [the fact] that it specified "the public domain" in connection with a basket more than the rest [of the items], for all of them also deal with the public domain; rather, it specified "the public domain" [to indicate] that in a courtyard it is permitted in every manner.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:1:1.hebrew: והוא שקשורה לו מע"ש - רש"י פי' לקמן, דבקשורה מע"ש הוי מלבוש החמור, אבל באינה קשורה מע"ש הוי משאוי. ועוד יש לפרש, דבאינה קשורה מע"ש מיחזי כמתכוין להוצאת המרדעת. וה"ר פור"ת פירש, דמיחזי כאילו מתכוין להוליך הבהמה למקום רחוק:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:1:1.english: "And that only applies where it was tied to it from Shabbat eve" - Rashi explained later in the chapter that when the saddlecloth is tied to it from Shabbat eve, it is the donkey's garment; but when it is not tied to it from Shabbat eve, it is a burden. And it can further be explained that when it is not tied to it from Shabbat eve, it appears as though one intends to carry out the saddlecloth. And Rabbeinu Porat explained that it appears as though one intends to lead the animal to a distant place.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:2:1.hebrew: אילימא שאינה קשורה לו כלל פשיטא - ולא בעי למפרך: דמרישא שמעינן לה, דקתני "בזמן שהיא קשורה", הא אינה קשורה — לא; דדרך משניות כן: במסכת ע"ז (דף לה:): "אלו דברים אסורין באכילה: כבשים שדרכן לתת לתוכן יין כו'", ובסיפא (שם דך לט:) קתני: "ואלו מותרים באכילה כו' וכבשים שאין דרכן לתת כו'", ובפרק אלו טרפות (חולין דף נד.) קתני: "אלו כשרות", אע"ג דאיכא מינייהו דשמעי' מרישא. וא"ת: ונפשוט מרישא דבקשורה מערב שבת איירי, מדאיצטריך למיתני "בזמן שהיא קשורה" — דבלאו הכי הוה ידעי' דאיירי בקשורה, דאי באינה קשורה, פשיטא דאסור, דילמא נפלה ואתי לאתויי, כדקאמר הכא: "אילימא כו'", אלא ודאי "בזמן שקשורה מע"ש" קאמר! וי"ל: דמרישא לא תפשוט, דאדרבה ה"א דלהכי תנא "בזמן שהיא קשורה" לאשמעי' דאפי' קשורה בשבת — דאי לא תנא ליה, ה"א: דוקא בקשורה לו מע"ש, אבל בקשורה בשבת לא, קמ"ל; להכי דייק מסיפא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:2:1.english: "If you say that it is not tied to it at all, that is obvious" - And [the Gemara] does not seek to object: "We [already] learn this from the first clause (the reisha), as it teaches: 'when it is tied to it' — [implying that] when it is not tied, no [it may not go out]!" For this is the way of Mishnayot: in tractate Avodah Zarah (35b): "These items are forbidden to be eaten: Preserves that are typically prepared with wine...", and in the latter clause (there, 39b) it teaches: "And these are permitted to be eaten... and preserves that are not typically prepared...", and in the chapter [entitled] Elu Tereifot (Chullin 54a) it teaches: "These are kosher," even though there are some of them that we [already] learn from the first clause. And if you say: Then let us resolve [the matter] from the first clause, [proving] that it is dealing with [a saddlecloth] that was tied from Shabbat eve, from the fact that it was necessary to teach "when it is tied to it" — for without this, we would have known that it is dealing with [a saddlecloth] that is tied, because if it were dealing with one that is not tied, it is obvious that it is forbidden lest it fall and he come to bring it, as [the Gemara] states here: "If you say...", etc.; rather, surely it means "when it was tied from Shabbat eve"! And one can say: From the first clause you cannot resolve it, for on the contrary, I would have said that it taught "when it is tied" for this reason: to teach us that even if it was tied on Shabbat [it is permitted] — for had it not taught this, I would have said: specifically when it was tied to it from Shabbat eve [is it permitted], but when it was tied on Shabbat, no, [it is not permitted]; thus it teaches us [that even if tied on Shabbat, it is permitted]. For this reason, [the Gemara] makes its deduction from the latter clause.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:4:1.hebrew: מהו ליתן המרדעת ע"ג חמור בשבת - ואין לאסור משום דאין כלי ניטל אלא לדבר הניטל, דבהמה חשיבא כדבר הניטל, כיון דיכול למושכה ולהוליכה בכל מקום. ורב אסי בר נתן דבעי אם אסור — אין לפרש משום דמיחזי כרוצה להוליך הבהמה למקום רחוק, דא"כ, היכי דייק דמאן דשרי טרסקל כ"ש מרדעת? ואין לפרש נמי דבעי למיסר בחצר אטו רה"ר, כדאמר גבי אשה בפ' במה אשה (לקמן שבת דף סד:), דגבי בהמה לא גזרו, כדתניא בסמוך גבי זוג: "ומטיילת עמו בחצר". אלא נראה לר"י דטעמא משום טרחא דשבת; ואע"ג דשריא קרצוף בפ"ב דביצה (דף כנ.) — התם יש לה צער ביותר, א"נ לא שרי אלא בי"ט, אבל בשבת אסור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:4:1.english: "What is [the law regarding] placing a saddlecloth on a donkey on Shabbat?" - And one cannot prohibit [this] on the grounds that a utensil may only be moved for the sake of an object that may be moved, for an animal is considered like an object that may be moved, since one can pull it and lead it anywhere. And as for Rav Asi bar Natan, who inquired whether it is prohibited — one cannot explain [that his question was] because it appears as though he wishes to lead the animal to a distant place; for if so, how does [the Gemara] infer that whoever permits a basket [of fodder], all the more so [permits] a saddlecloth? And one also cannot explain that he sought to prohibit [it even] in a courtyard on account of the public domain, as [the Gemara] says regarding a woman in the chapter [entitled] "Bameh Ishah" (below, Shabbat 64b), for regarding an animal they did not enact a decree, as is taught nearby regarding a bell: "and she may walk about with it in a courtyard." Rather, it appears to the Ri that the reason is due to exertion on Shabbat. And even though currying was permitted in the second chapter of Beitza (23a) — there it experiences greater suffering; alternatively, it was permitted only on Yom Tov, but on Shabbat it is prohibited.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:5:1.hebrew: אוכף שע"ג החמור - וא"ת: ויתיר האוכף וינער ויפול, כדאמר בפ' כל כתבי גבי "היתה בהמתו טעונה טבל כו'"? וי"ל: דהתם מיירי בשקין, שתוכל הבהמה להתקלקל; אבל מחמת האוכף לא תוכל הבהמה להתקלקל, לכך לא התירו:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:5:1.english: "A saddle that is on a donkey" - And if you will say: Let him untie the saddle and shake [it], and it will fall off, as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Kol Kitvei regarding: "If one's animal was laden with tevel [untithed produce]," etc.? And one can say: There it is dealing with sacks, where the animal could be harmed; but on account of the saddle, the animal cannot be harmed, [and] therefore they did not permit [it].

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:6:1.hebrew: תולין טרסקל - וא"ת: ותאסר משום דמשתמש בבע"ח, כי היכי דאסור להניח נר על גבי דקל בשבת משום דמשתמש במחובר? וי"ל: דהתם מנענע הענפים, אבל הכא אינו מנענע הבהמה בכך. ורב אסי ברבי נתן דבעי למיסר אפסר — משום דילמא אתי להשתמש בבע"ח (ת".):
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:6:1.english: "One may hang a basket" - And if you say: But let it be prohibited because of using an animal, just as it is prohibited to place a lamp on a palm tree on Shabbat because of using [something] attached [to the ground]? And one can say: There, one shakes the branches, but here, one does not shake the animal by doing so. And Rav Asi bar Rabbi Natan, who wanted to prohibit a halter, [did so] lest one come to make use of an animal (Tos.).

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:8:1.hebrew: אריוך - שם מלך, כדכתיב: "אריוך מלך אלסר" (בראסית יד). ונקטי' טפי משאר מלכים — לפי שמובלע בו לשון ארי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:8:1.english: Aryokh - [This is] the name of a king, as it is written: "Aryoch king of Ellasar" (Genesis 14:1). And [it] chose [this name] over other kings because the word ari [lion] is embedded in it.

Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:9:1.hebrew: דשמעיה דקא מסיים בה כו' - אע"ג דקיי"ל כרב באיסורי, היינו לגבי שמואל לחודיה; אבל הכא, ר' יוחנן — דקי"ל כוותיה לגבי רב — קאי כשמואל. וברייתא דאוכף נמי קיימא כשמואל, למאי דמשני: "כאן לחממה, כאן לצננה". ומתני' ד"אין סכין ומפרכסין לבהמה" דמייתי לקמן, נמי פליגא אדרב, כדפירש בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Shabbat 53a:9:1.english: "That he heard him conclude with it, etc." - Even though we maintain that the halakha is like Rav in [matters of] prohibitions, that is only regarding [a dispute with] Shmuel alone. But here, Rabbi Yoḥanan — whom we hold like against Rav — stands like Shmuel. And the baraita of the saddle also stands like Shmuel, according to what [the Gemara] answers: "Here to warm it, here to cool it." And the Mishnah [teaching] that "one may not smear [oil] or scrape [scabs] for an animal," which [the Gemara] cites later, also disagrees with Rav, as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres.
